chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from al-Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (AS)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' He replied, 'His Knowledge.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Kursi of Allah extend over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a precise theological interpretation of the Kursi, identifying it not as a physical entity but as the expansive domain of Divine Knowledge (Ilm). This explanation aligns with the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* by distinguishing between Allah’s attributes and His essence, thereby avoiding anthropomorphic conceptions of the divine throne. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding how scriptural descriptions of 'space' or 'extent' often refer to the breadth of God's awareness and power rather than material dimensions.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyah that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: His knowledge extends over the heaves and the earth.’ He replied, “His Knowledge.”
